mechanism: Ketorolac (NSAID) increases GI bleeding risk and may impair renal function; prochlorperazine can mask GI symptoms and increase anticholinergic effects that reduce gastric motility, compounding GI injury risk.
action: Avoid concurrent use if possible; if necessary, use lowest ketorolac dose for shortest duration and monitor for GI symptoms, renal function, and signs of GI bleeding.
